title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Ecology — 2023
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Define ecosystem. Describe the structure of an ecosystem with a diagram.
questions.solution:
**Ecosystem:** A community of organisms interacting with their physical environment.

**Structure:**
- **Abiotic:** Temperature, light, water, soil, nutrients
- **Biotic:** Producers (plants), Consumers (herbivores, carnivores), Decomposers (bacteria, fungi)

Trophic levels: Producers → Primary consumers → Secondary consumers → Tertiary consumers
Decomposers recycle nutrients from all levels.
questions.knowledgeNote: Energy flows one-way in ecosystems (10% rule); nutrients cycle.
questions.answer: **Ecosystem:** the basic functional unit of nature — **a biotic community (all the living organisms) interacting with its abiotic environment** (light, water, soil, air, temperature) in a defined area, through which **energy flows and nutrients cycle** (Tansley, 1935). A pond, a forest and a grassland are all ecosystems. **Structure of an ecosystem (with diagram description):** **(1) Abiotic components:** inorganic substances (C, N, H₂O, minerals), organic matter (humus) and climatic factors (light, temperature, rainfall) — the raw materials and physical stage. **(2) Biotic components by function:** • **Producers (autotrophs):** green plants and algae that capture solar energy by photosynthesis and build organic matter — the entry gate of energy into the ecosystem. • **Consumers (heterotrophs):** animals that eat other organisms — **primary consumers** (herbivores: deer, tadpoles), **secondary consumers** (carnivores eating herbivores: frog), **tertiary consumers** (top carnivores: tiger, snake). • **Decomposers (saprotrophs):** bacteria and fungi breaking down dead matter, returning nutrients to the abiotic pool — the recycling arm. **Diagram description:** a pond or grassland scene — sun's rays striking green plants (producers); arrows from plants to herbivorous insects/tadpoles (primary consumers), onward to frogs/fish (secondary consumers) and to top carnivores; dead leaves and carcasses arrowing down to bacteria and fungi (decomposers), with arrows from decomposers back to the soil/water (nutrients) and back into the plants — a circular nutrient loop with a one-way energy arrow from sun to plants to consumers, lost as heat at each step. **Deep point:** the structure is two loops — a closed **nutrient circle** and an open **energy line** that enters at the sun and leaves as heat; the ecosystem lives in the tension between the two.

questions.question: Differentiate between the pyramid of numbers and the pyramid of biomass, and state one case in which each becomes inverted.
questions.solution:
**Pyramid of numbers** shows the **number of individual organisms** present at each successive trophic level.
- It **depends on the size of the organism**, so its shape changes with the ecosystem.
- In a **grassland** it is **upright**: grass (many) → grasshopper (fewer) → frog (few) → snake (fewest).
- In a **tree ecosystem** it becomes **spindle-shaped**: one huge banyan tree → many herbivorous insects → a few insectivorous birds → a few hawks.
- In a **parasitic food chain** it is **completely inverted**: a single tree → one *Mistletoe* → several lice → millions of bacteria.

**Pyramid of biomass** shows the **standing crop (dry mass)** of living material at each trophic level, usually in g m⁻² or kg m⁻².
- It is **always upright in terrestrial ecosystems** because the mass of each trophic level is less than the level below it.
- It becomes **inverted in an aquatic ecosystem**: phytoplankton (very small standing crop) → zooplankton (larger) → small fish → large fish, because the phytoplankton reproduce and are eaten so rapidly that their **turnover rate is very high**, so their standing crop at any instant is small.
- In a grassland plot the biomass of insects and earthworms may exceed that of the grass, giving a partly upright or spindle-shaped pyramid.

**Contrast:** the pyramid of numbers counts individuals, whereas the pyramid of biomass measures total living mass; only the pyramid of energy is always upright.
questions.knowledgeNote: Pyramid of numbers can invert in a tree ecosystem; pyramid of biomass can invert in water because phytoplankton have a very high turnover rate.
questions.answer: **Pyramid of numbers:** a bar diagram showing the **count of individual organisms** at each trophic level (producers at the base, top carnivore at the apex). Usually upright (many plants, fewer herbivores, fewer carnivores), but **inverted when one large individual supports many parasites** — e.g. **one large tree supporting thousands of insects** and their parasites: numbers increase upward. **Pyramid of biomass:** bars show the **total dry weight (standing crop)** of organisms at each level. Upright in most terrestrial ecosystems (plant biomass > herbivore biomass > carnivore biomass), but **inverted in aquatic ecosystems** — e.g. in a pond the **standing biomass of phytoplankton at a moment can be less than that of the fish** feeding on them, because the tiny algae turn over so fast. **Differences:** numbers count *heads*, biomass weighs *flesh*; numbers invert for a single large producer, biomass inverts for fast-turnover producers. **Deep point:** neither pyramid can invert the **pyramid of energy** — energy is lost at every transfer, so only the energy pyramid is always upright; the other two measure snapshots, energy measures the flow.
